ordered_diagnoses: Nonkeratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal mucosa with Schneiderian features

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lesion of the nasal vestibule with local invasion
salient_findings: Recurrence of the lesion after excision
Tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
Never-smoker
Initial lesion on the right nasal vestibule mucosa
Initial biopsy showed solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative on initial biopsy
Recurrence of the lesion 8 months after initial presentation
Second excision showed p63 positive and p16 negative with positive margins
Imaging showed thicker right ala compared to the left ala
Tumor extended into the floor of the nasal vestibule
Microscopic examination showed downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes

shortlist: Nonkeratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal mucosa with Schneiderian features

shortlist.label: Malignant hidradenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Initial diagnosis of solid and cystic hidradenoma with recurrence

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to malignant hidradenoma, with aggressive behavior

shortlist.label: Nonkeratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal mucosa with Schneiderian features

raw.rationale: The microscopic examination showing downward papillomatous proliferation of small, uniform, slightly atypical keratinocytes is consistent with inverted papilloma, and the recurrence and extension of the tumor into the nasal vestibule floor also support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of clear evidence of squamous cell carcinoma features such as significant atypia or invasion makes it less likely

rejected.label: Malignant hidradenoma
rejected.why: The initial biopsy was reported as a benign hidradenoma, and the recurrence does not necessarily indicate malignancy

rejected.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to malignant hidradenoma, the evidence does not strongly support a diagnosis of hidradenocarcinoma

rejected.label: Nonkeratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the nasal mucosa with Schneiderian features
rejected.why: The microscopic features and clinical presentation do not specifically suggest this rare and distinct entity
